bmt-2016-discrete-01.title: Weighted average
bmt-2016-discrete-01.body:
Let there be $q$ quarters and $k$ nickels. The average is $\frac{25q+5k}{q+k}=10$, so $25q+5k=10q+10k$, i.e. $15q=5k$ and $k=3q$. The bag has at least one quarter (otherwise the average is $5$), so $q\ge1$ and $k\ge3$. With $1$ quarter and $3$ nickels the average is $\frac{25+15}{4}=10$. 

**Answer: 3**

bmt-2016-discrete-02.title: Inclusion-exclusion
bmt-2016-discrete-02.body:
Multiples of $3$: $672$; of $7$: $288$; of $21$: $96$ (and $2016=21\cdot96$). Numbers divisible by exactly one of $3,7$: $(672-96)+(288-96)=576+192=768$. (Those divisible by $21$ are divisible by both and are excluded.)

**Answer: 768**

bmt-2016-discrete-03.title: Choose ranks and suits
bmt-2016-discrete-03.body:
Pick the rank of the triple ($13$ ways) and which $3$ of its $4$ suits ($\binom43=4$), then the rank of the pair ($12$ ways) and its $2$ suits ($\binom42=6$): $13\cdot4\cdot12\cdot6=3744$.

**Answer: 3744**

bmt-2016-discrete-04.title: Set up the flow of socks
bmt-2016-discrete-04.body:
Each person starts with $3$ socks and ends with $3$ socks. Call the people $A,B,C$, and let $x$ be the number of $A$'s socks that go to $B$ (so $3-x$ go to $C$). Column and row sums being $3$ forces: the number going $A\to B$, $B\to C$, $C\to A$ all equal $x$, and $A\to C$, $C\to B$, $B\to A$ all equal $3-x$. (E.g. $B$ receives $x$ from $A$ and must receive $3-x$ from $C$; $C$ gives $3-x$ to $B$ so gives $x$ to $A$, and so on.)

Given $x$, each person chooses which $x$ of their $3$ socks go to the next person in the cycle $A\to B\to C\to A$: $\binom3x^3$ ways. Total: $\sum_{x=0}^3\binom3x^3=1+27+27+1=56$.

**Answer: 56**

bmt-2016-discrete-05.title: Reduce the exponent
bmt-2016-discrete-05.body:
$9^{10}=3486784401\equiv01\pmod{100}$, so the exponent only matters mod $10$. Let $E=8^{7^{\cdots^2}}$. Powers of $8$ mod $10$ cycle $8,4,2,6$ with period $4$, so we need $7^{6^{\cdots}}\bmod4$: $7\equiv-1$ and the exponent $6^{\cdots}$ is even, so it is $\equiv1\pmod4$. Hence $E\equiv8^1=8\pmod{10}$ and the number is $\equiv9^8=43046721\equiv21\pmod{100}$.

**Answer: 21**

bmt-2016-discrete-06.title: Chain strategy and an upper bound
bmt-2016-discrete-06.body:
For positive numbers $t_1\ge t_2\ge\dots\ge t_n$ let $L(t)=\sum_k2^{n-k}t_k$. We claim the maximum final value is $L(t)$.

Achievable: keep one running number, starting from $t_1$ and each time $v\mapsto 2v+t_{k}$ with the next largest; the result is $2^{n-1}t_1+2^{n-2}t_2+\dots+t_n$ (check: $2t_1+t_2$, then $4t_1+2t_2+t_3$, ...).

Upper bound by induction on $n$: if the first move replaces $x,y$ by $z=2x+y$, the new list has $n-1$ numbers and by induction the final value is at most $L(\text{new})$. By the rearrangement inequality $L(\text{new})$ equals the best pairing of the new list with weights $2^{n-2},\dots,1$. Take that optimal ordering; replace $z$ (weight $w$) by $x$ and $y$ placed in consecutive positions with weights $2w$ and $w$ in the old list (the numbers before $z$ get doubled weights, those after keep theirs). This ordering has value at least the new value, since $2wx+wy=wz$ and the others only increase. Therefore $L(\text{old})\ge L(\text{new})$, and the final value is at most $L(\text{old})$.

With $t_k=n+1-k$: $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(j+1)2^j=(n-1)2^n+1$.

**Answer: $2^n(n-1)+1$**

bmt-2016-discrete-07.title: Clique and coloring
bmt-2016-discrete-07.body:
The vertices $v_1,v_2,v_4,\dots,v_{512}$ are pairwise adjacent (each divides the next), a clique of size $10$, so at least $10$ colors are needed.

Conversely color $v_n$ by $\Omega(n)$, the number of prime factors counted with multiplicity. If $i\mid j$ and $i<j$ then $\Omega(i)<\Omega(j)$, so adjacent vertices get different colors. Since $2^{10}=1024>1000$, $\Omega(n)\le9$, giving values $0,\dots,9$: $10$ colors suffice.

**Answer: 10**

bmt-2016-discrete-08.title: Bound and equality
bmt-2016-discrete-08.body:
Lower bound: for every edge $uv$, $x_ux_v\ge-\frac{x_u^2+x_v^2}{2}$. Each vertex lies on $n$ edges, so summing over edges gives $S\ge-\frac n2\sum x_i^2$.

Equality: the hypercube is bipartite (by parity of the number of $1$s). Put $x_v=1$ on even vertices and $-1$ on odd ones; every edge then has label $-1$, so $S=-n2^{n-1}$ while $\sum x_i^2=2^n$, giving $-\frac n2$.

**Answer: $-\frac n2$**

bmt-2016-discrete-09.title: Conjugates
bmt-2016-discrete-09.body:
Let $\alpha=(\sqrt6+\sqrt7)^2=13+2\sqrt{42}$ and $\bar\alpha=13-2\sqrt{42}\in(0,1)$. Then $N_k=\alpha^k+\bar\alpha^k$ is an integer with $N_0=2$, $N_1=26$, $N_k=26N_{k-1}-N_{k-2}$ (since $\alpha\bar\alpha=1$ and $\alpha+\bar\alpha=26$).

$(\sqrt6+\sqrt7)^{1000}=\alpha^{500}=N_{500}-\bar\alpha^{500}$, which is slightly below the integer $N_{500}$; so its integer part is $N_{500}-1$. Running the recurrence modulo $100$ (it is periodic, so this is a short computation) gives $N_{500}\equiv74\pmod{100}$, so the last two digits are $73$.

**Answer: 73**

bmt-2016-discrete-10.title: Fault-free tilings
bmt-2016-discrete-10.body:
Such tilings are "fault-free". A $5\times6$ rectangle has one; label each domino by a number:

```
 1  1  2  2  3  4
 5  6  6  7  3  4
 5  8  9  7 10 10
11  8  9 12 12 13
11 14 14 15 15 13
```

Every one of the $4$ horizontal and $5$ vertical grid lines is crossed by a domino. For smaller areas ($mn\in\{4,6,\dots,28\}$, $m,n\ge2$ since a $1\times n$ strip with $n>2$ always splits) one checks all tilings of each rectangle (small by hand, or by computer search) and every tiling has a fault line. So the minimum is $30$.

**Answer: 30**
